copy.blurb:
A +19.4pp gap on the Argentina side. Argentina v Austria in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Argentina stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Public Elo rates Argentina 310 points higher than the other side (Argentina 2140, Austria 1830). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Argentina to win at 76%, the draw at 11%, and Austria to win at 13%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Argentina sits at 76% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Argentina to win at 56%, the draw at 24%, and Austria to win at 17%. Kalshi has Argentina at 56%, which prices out at American odds of −130; the model has the same side at 76%. The +19.4pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Argentina, that haircut lands the model at 66%; the market is at 56%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +9.8pp. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 31 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
